entities.summary:
Boniface II was a prominent entrepreneur and business leader of the Classical era, active in Rome from approximately 470 to 532 CE. He is known for his significant contributions to the development of the city's infrastructure, including the construction of several public buildings and roads.

    As a religious figure, Boniface II played a crucial role in the establishment of several churches and monasteries throughout the region. His efforts to promote Christianity and spread the teachings of the early Church Fathers had a lasting impact on the spiritual landscape of the Western world.

    Despite his many achievements, Boniface II's legacy was not without controversy. His business dealings and political machinations often put him at odds with his contemporaries, leading to a complex and often tumultuous personal life. Nevertheless, his influence on the course of Roman history cannot be overstated.

    The exact date of Boniface II's death is unknown, but it is believed to have occurred sometime between 532 and 10th of September.
